prompt: Users upload photos and videos up to 4 GB each. The relational database is growing by a terabyte a week.
why: Put the files in object storage (S3, GCS) and keep only their keys and metadata in the database.
trap: Sharding the database just spreads huge blobs over more databases.

prompt: Large video uploads pass through your app servers and tie them up for minutes.
why: Hand out pre-signed URLs so clients upload straight to object storage.
trap: More app servers behind a balancer still waste them on byte shuffling.

prompt: Nightly database backups of 2 TB must be kept for seven years at low cost.
tells: kept for seven years at low cost
why: Object storage with lifecycle rules to move old backups to archival tiers.
trap: A replica is a live copy, not a 7-year history.

prompt: Data scientists share 500 GB training datasets that never change once written.
why: Large immutable files are exactly what object storage is for.
trap: Caching assumes small hot items, not half-terabyte files.
